questions: Does current ClayGraph activation justify FRANK hot-path use?
Is current latency intrinsic to graph semantics or implementation/indexing?
When should graph retrieval be used relative to exact/packet/FTS retrieval?

evidence_surfaces.finding: current graph/graph-lexical roughly 84-87ms median/query vs SQLite FTS ~0.8-0.9ms; graph contexts larger; some relational facts surfaced; activation not consistently better than graph lexical
reload+scan 20.499ms median; resident scan 8.349ms; resident inverted seed index 0.106ms
graph benefit is conditional on complexity/scattered evidence; routing simple queries to cheaper retrieval is a current independent research direction

decision_effect: Current activation is rejected as already-hot-path-ready. Semantic graph retained. Preferred HOLD candidate becomes G1c resident adaptive escalation.
answer_change: Yes. Before the imported 8B test, the main uncertainty was whether G1b selection quality could beat baselines. After the 8B test, hot-path latency/context cost becomes a first-class blocker and the candidate architecture changes from graph-first query planning to baseline-first adaptive graph escalation with resident indexes.
limitations: runner timing is not live FRANK
local index benchmark is synthetic and excludes full provenance/traversal/update costs
no current-corpus G1c implementation benchmark yet
